memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then put in the ark the tablets of the covenant law, which I will give you." - Exodus 25:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God instructs that the tablets of the covenant law be placed inside the ark — the most sacred container in Israel, kept in the most holy place. His commandments were not to be tossed aside or treated casually. They were treasured, protected, kept at the very centre of the nation's worship and life.

The placement preaches a sermon. God's Word belonged at the heart of everything, not at the edges. Israel's identity, worship, and daily life were meant to revolve around what God had spoken. The law was not a burden shoved in a corner; it was a treasure kept in the holiest place they had.

Where do we keep God's Word? For many of us, Scripture sits at the periphery of life — consulted occasionally, squeezed in when convenient, respected in theory but not central in practice. God invites us to something better: to treasure His Word at the very centre of who we are. The psalmist put it beautifully: "I have hidden your word in my heart that I might not sin against you" (Ps 119:11). And under the new covenant, God does something even greater — He writes His law not on stone kept in a box, but on our hearts (Heb 8:10). Let His Word live there, treasured and central.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is God's Word at the centre of my life, or somewhere at the edges?
What would it look like to genuinely treasure Scripture this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for keeping Your Word at the edges of my life. Write it deep on my heart and let it sit at the very centre of who I am and how I live. Amen.
